digest.component_or_area: inbound-probe dispatch chain / binding store / outbound differ
propositions: The (inbound, probe) dispatch chain has no live producer: differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes only emits when local_state entries carry jira_key, but run_differs passes a fetched Jira snapshot whose entries never carry jira_key, so the loop never fires in production.

Deletion vs aged-out discrimination is already live twice: outbound_differ._safe_get_issue maps 404→_DELETED (verified on real DC); binding_walk.py:187-196 performs bounded GET for off-snapshot bindings and maps to four-way state including CONFIRMED_404.

Without a retirement guard, a local ticket whose binding was retired on confirmed 404 is re-created in Jira via outbound_differ.py:502-513 (eventual resurrection after grace period), contradicting the operator ruling that deleted items must not be resurrected.

The resurrection implementation (c244's same-pass re-create via _apply_inbound_delete→create_after_hard_delete) is inert because route_inbound_probe (the sole producer of (inbound, delete)) never runs without an (inbound, probe) input.

The dead chain must be deleted and replaced with a tombstone guard: BindingStore.is_retired_local prevents unbound-create emission for tickets with a retired binding, making resurrection opt-in via BindingStore.unretire rather than automatic.

The suppression must be observable and reversible: note_create_suppressed raises a bridge alert naming local_id, retired jira_key, and unretire(key) as the remedy; unretire drops the key from both memory and bindings-retired.json.
